# Cost model results (generated by `models/cost_model.py`)

All figures USD/month unless stated, excluding VAT/sales tax. Prices dated 2026-10-12 ([S044] Anthropic, [S045] OpenAI, [S046] Google, [S071] Intercom). Labour: BLS May 2025 medians [S077][S078] × 1.4 loaded-cost ASSUMPTION → support $30.14/h, engineer $15,864/FTE-month; contractor $90/h ASSUMPTION.

|---|---|---|
| claude-haiku-5.5 | 0.0108 | 169,200 |
| claude-sonnet-5.5 | 0.2049 | 169,200 |
| claude-opus-5.5 | 0.4098 | 169,200 |

Same loop on claude-sonnet-5.5 with **no cache hits**: 0.4545 $/task (vs 0.2049 at 80% hit) — caching is the largest free lever.

## Scenario 1 — Personal agent (API pay-as-you-go vs subscription)

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| low | 150 | $10.92 | $0.00 | $10.92 | $0.07 | 99% | 1.2 | 7.5 |
| base | 450 | $157 | $6.00 | $163 | $0.38 | 96% | 7.5 | 128.7 |
| high | 1200 | $4,600 | $25.00 | $4,625 | $4.39 | 88% | 40.0 | 3483.0 |

Comparison: Claude Pro $20/mo, Max from $100/mo [S047] (flat, but with rolling 5-hour and weekly usage limits; subscription credentials may **not** be used by third-party agent harnesses [S016]).

Model-choice sensitivity for the base personal case:

| Model | Total $/mo |

| claude-haiku-5.5 | $19.40 |
| claude-sonnet-5.5 | $163 |
| claude-opus-5.5 | $315 |
| claude-fable-5.1 | $750 |
| gpt-5.5 | $374 |
| gemini-3.1-pro | $156 |

*Model swap holds success rate constant — in reality cheaper models usually fail more on long tasks, which raises cost per success (see METR/RLI evidence in the paper).*

Base total $135,304: LLM tokens are 8%, human escalations 74%, fixed engineering/infra/security 17%. The resolution rate, not the token price, dominates economics.

### Break-even resolution rate (base build case)

- resolve 20%: total $194,458 vs human-only $200,947 → saving 3%
- resolve 30%: total $174,740 vs human-only $200,947 → saving 13%
- resolve 40%: total $155,022 vs human-only $200,947 → saving 23%
- resolve 50%: total $135,304 vs human-only $200,947 → saving 33%
- resolve 60%: total $115,586 vs human-only $200,947 → saving 42%
- resolve 70%: total $95,869 vs human-only $200,947 → saving 52%

## Labour-cost jurisdiction sensitivity (v1.1)

Eurostat hourly labour cost levels, 2025, whole economy excl. public administration, all-in employer cost (lc_lci_lev, D1_D4_MD5) [S119]: EU27 €34.9, Germany €45.0, Estonia €21.1, Latvia €16.3. Converted at 1.1206 USD/EUR (ECB, 2026-10-09). **Caveat:** whole-economy averages, not support-agent wages. The US figure is the occupation-specific BLS median × 1.4 (ASSUMPTION).

| Labour cost basis | $/hour | Production base: total $/month | Human-only baseline | Saving | Small-business base: total | Human-only | Saving |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| US support agent (BLS × 1.4) | 30.14 | $135,304 | $200,947 | 33% | $6,159 | $12,057 | 49% |
| EU27 average | 39.11 | $165,755 | $260,726 | 36% | $7,616 | $15,644 | 51% |
| Germany average | 50.43 | $204,189 | $336,180 | 39% | $9,455 | $20,171 | 53% |
| Estonia average | 23.64 | $113,240 | $157,631 | 28% | $5,103 | $9,458 | 46% |
| Latvia average | 18.27 | $94,975 | $121,772 | 22% | $4,229 | $7,306 | 42% |

## Occupation-adjusted labour and local engineering (v1.2)

CALCULATION: all-in labour cost [S119] × (occupation mean hourly earnings ÷ all-occupation mean) from the 2022 Structure of Earnings Survey [S126]. Clerical support workers (ISCO 4) stand in for support agents; professionals (ISCO 2) for engineers, at 160 paid hours/month (ASSUMPTION). Ratios: clerical EU27 15.83/17.69, DE 20.03/22.23, LV 7.67/9.17; professionals EU27 24.40/17.69, DE 32.37/22.23, LV 13.04/9.17. Earnings ratios are applied to labour costs (ASSUMPTION: employer on-costs proportional).

| Jurisdiction | Support $/h (clerical-adjusted) | Engineer $/month (local) | Production base saving: US engineering | Production base saving: local engineering |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EU27 | 35.00 | 8,631 | 35% | 38% |
| Germany | 45.44 | 11,749 | 38% | 40% |
| Latvia | 15.28 | 4,156 | 17% | 28% |

INTERPRETATION (v1.2): using support-type (clerical) rather than whole-economy labour lowers the human cost replaced, and so the saving; hiring engineers locally raises it again. The direction of the v1.1 finding holds: the same deployment saves a smaller share in Latvia than in Germany.


INTERPRETATION: cheaper labour shrinks the *percentage* saving from automation, because fixed engineering, security and model costs are priced globally (in USD) while the human work replaced is cheaper. An EU/Latvia-based deployment therefore needs a higher resolution rate to beat an all-human team than a US one. Engineering FTE is held at the US BLS rate in every row; with local engineering salaries the gap narrows (not modelled).
